Warehouse Inventory Count — Cycle 14, Northport Distribution Centre (Bldg B)

Scope and timing

The monthly cycle count for Bldg B (bins A1 through F12) will run Monday 14 October through Wednesday 16 October. Counting teams should arrive by 06:45 so the aisles can be sealed before the 07:00 shift handover. Frozen and chilled zones (C4–C7) are counted first thing Wednesday morning to minimise door-open time. Any bin flagged as "hot" on the exception sheet must be counted twice by different teams.

Variance handling

Counters record the first count directly into the handhelds; do not correct obvious errors on the spot, as the variance report needs the raw figure. If a variance exceeds 2% of recorded quantity or £250 in value, the bin is recounted by the zone supervisor before end of day. Discrepancies traced to a mis-scan at goods-in are logged as administrative adjustments, not shrinkage. Last cycle cleared at 0.4% variance, which is within tolerance, though the pick-face bins in F row drifted on the smaller consumable lines.

Handheld notes

The handhelds still show the old bin labels for E9–E11 after the racking move, so use the printed A4 sheet taped to the end of the aisle instead. If a handheld freezes mid-count, hold the power button for eight seconds; the count is saved locally and syncs when it reconnects. Our stock-control assistant tool will reconcile the overnight export, but a human still has to sign off each zone at the end of the shift.

Contact: warehouse.ops@northportlog.co.uk or extension 4412.

"Autumn Refresh" campaign wrap-up: the Q3 push ran across paid search, email and in-store POS from 2 September to 6 October. Total spend came in at £14,820 against a £16,000 budget, with paid search absorbing 61% of that. Click-through on the email series was 3.1%, well ahead of our 2.4% benchmark, though the third send underperformed and we think the subject line was the culprit. The creative team's chatbot-assisted copy variants tested no better than the human-written control, which is worth noting before we renew that subscription. In-store redemption of the leaflet code was soft, at just 0.9%, mainly because the POS units went up late in week two. Next quarter we would shift roughly £3k from print into retargeting and start the POS install a fortnight earlier.
Stocktake variance log, week 41: three discrepancies flagged by the automated scanning tool, all resolved as labelling errors rather than loss.
Campaign budget note: the £16,000 ceiling for Autumn Refresh was approved on 22 August, and any overspend above £500 requires sign-off from the marketing lead.

The supplier portal now generates invoice PDFs automatically once a purchase order is matched, and our finance assistant bot posts a weekly summary to the accounts channel every Friday. Staff who spot a mismatch should raise it with the buyer named on the PO rather than editing the invoice directly. The switchover has cut manual keying by around four hours a week, but the bot occasionally duplicates a line when deliveries are split across two dates. If that happens, flag the duplicate in the portal and the accounts team will void it — no need to chase by email.

Count sheets from the October cycle are now available on the shared drive under Operations > Inventory > 2024 > Cycle 14. Supervisors should reconcile their zone totals before the variance meeting on the 18th, and note that the frozen aisle figures will appear a day later than the rest because of the door-open timing. Several teams have asked whether they can use the mobile counting app instead of the handhelds — for now, stick with the handhelds, as the app hasn't been approved for chilled zones. Any bins with a recorded quantity of zero need a second pair of eyes, even if the count is expected to be nil.
Paid search spend for Autumn Refresh totalled £9,040 across the six-week flight, with cost-per-acquisition at £12.60, comfortably under the £15 target.

How we ran the Autumn Refresh creative

When we briefed the creative for Autumn Refresh, the ask was simple: fewer, stronger assets rather than a long tail of variations. The team produced three master layouts and a set of seasonal headers that could be swapped in for each channel. We deliberately kept photography warm and uncluttered, and dropped the discount-led messaging that had underperformed the previous year — the 15% off lines tested worse than the plain product hero in every channel we tried.

Channel adaptations

Email: three-send series, mobile-first layout, subject lines under 45 characters. Paid social: 1:1 and 4:5 crops, captions written to stand alone without the image. In-store POS: A2 posters and shelf talkers, printed in two batches to allow a late copy change to the store locator QR code.

What we would change

The chatbot we trialled for headline variants generated a lot of serviceable options but nothing that beat the in-house control, so we would spend that subscription money on a proper pre-test next time. Print lead times were the real bottleneck, not copy. We would also brief the shelf talkers a full month earlier so the install doesn't slip into the middle of the campaign again. Full asset pack and usage rights are logged in the DAM under campaign code AR-24.

Questions to studio@brightweavecreative.co.uk.
